purpose: Reproduce the research in a separate scratch workspace while retaining immutable original receipts.

environment.storage_and_primary_native_queries: GuavaJam Python 3.12.12, SQLite 3.50.4, locked workspace dependencies
environment.pandoc: 3.12.1 for source parsing; not needed when reusing retained NAV fixture
environment.proffer_validator: Python 3.12.14 / jsonschema 4.26.0; pinned schema/checker in tooling/proffer

setup: Read guides/corpus.json and guides/transport.json for exact pinned setup. Use a separate clean GuavaJam checkout at the tested base, not the reference commit.
Install GuavaJam locked Python dependencies and npm ci dependencies in that separate checkout. Install Chromium explicitly and pass its absolute executable path.
For chunks, run npm ci --prefix <reference>/experiments/range-http --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund. The lockfile pins sqlite-wasm-http 1.2.0 and fflate 0.8.2.
Keep generated DBs and new measurements outside the reference payload. Retained gzip corpus avoids regenerating the Riverhog native atlas.
primary_commands: Repeat storage and chunks with --editions 5, using the same scratch root or a new one. The original five-edition experiment did not run the full 38-case query matrix or complete production-worker matrix.
runner_status: reproduce.py is publication-time orchestration of the retained, measured scripts. Its dry-run CLI was checked; it was not the command used for the original experiments. Recorded commands and raw receipts remain the evidence of those runs.
comparability: Use exact input/source/harness hashes to establish identity. SQLite/zlib/Node versions can change binary output or timings; do not silently relabel a different build as the retained fixture.
A reproduced run writes new results. Never overwrite or reinterpret original shared-host measurements as stable p95 estimates.

Current and five-edition storage layouts have all field/occurrence integrity checks; source fidelity and the complete query/worker matrices were run for the current fixture. Five-edition browser cases were broad/selective/negative first-page searches.
Evidence-window excerpts intentionally differ; matching, rank, source occurrence and citation do not. See guides/search.json for the separate evidence commands.
Fifty-edition observations are text-payload sensitivity only. No 50-edition FTS/browser qualification is claimed.
Older native-heading supplemental receipts have different corpus/layout hashes and are labeled separately. Their files are not interchangeable with the final production-NAV fixture.
The source/build streaming patch is an independent prototype. The storage builder retains the corpus and converts an intermediate baseline DB; it is not the proposed bounded production builder.
runner_browser_scope: The browser convenience phase runs three transport cases. For one edition it also runs the 15-message unchanged-worker matrix across three layouts and the directory transport cases. For five editions it skips the full production-worker matrix because baseline/compact exceed the unchanged 256 MiB load bound; a single remaining layout cannot establish cross-layout parity.
